name: The Steading
tagline: An AI agent ecosystem, mapped as a working farm.
note: 15 of the 51 roles are live as Claude Code subagents in .claude/agents/, working today with no API keys. The Market is the only zone that faces a customer — it is where the farm stops costing money and starts making it. The rest are charters.

steward.label: Steward
steward.use: Owns outcomes. Plans, decomposes, arbitrates, decides when to stop.

specialist.label: Specialist
specialist.use: Deep single-domain judgment. Quality bar matters more than cost.

hand.label: Hand
hand.use: Bulk execution under a clear spec. The workhorses.

sorter.label: Sorter
sorter.use: Classify, route, extract, score. High volume, low ceremony.

task.label: Task
task.desc: A unit of work moving toward whoever will do it.

artifact.label: Artifact
artifact.desc: Produced output moving toward storage or delivery.

memory.label: Memory
memory.desc: Facts, episodes, and procedures moving in or out of store.

signal.label: Signal
signal.desc: Telemetry, health, and cost moving toward the watch.

zones.name: The Farmhouse
zones.subtitle: Command Yard
zones.charter: Receives intent from the outside world, turns it into a plan, and decides who does what. Nothing self-assigns on this farm; work is handed out here.
zones.failsWhen: It holds context for every worker at once and runs out of room to think. Past four concurrent crews, delegate to a Row Boss instead of tracking rows yourself.

zones.name: The Fields
zones.subtitle: The Rows
zones.charter: Where the actual labour happens, in parallel rows. A field runs one kind of work at scale: prepare, generate, extract, reduce. Rows do not talk to each other.
zones.failsWhen: Rows are given work that depends on other rows. Independence is the whole reason the field is fast; a dependency between rows turns a field into a queue.

zones.name: The Barn
zones.subtitle: Barnyard
zones.charter: Home to everything that stays alive between requests: durable sessions, scheduled jobs, and the supervisors that keep them honest. Fields forget; the barn remembers.
zones.failsWhen: A long-running agent is left unsupervised. Anything that can run for an hour can loop for an hour — the Sheepdog is not optional.

zones.name: The Silo Row
zones.subtitle: Granary
zones.charter: Four kinds of remembering, kept in four separate stores on purpose. Mixing them is the most common reason an agent ecosystem slowly goes senile.
zones.failsWhen: Everything is thrown into one vector store. Vectors are good at 'something like this' and bad at 'what happened, in what order' — keep the trace separate from the facts.

zones.name: The Toolshed
zones.subtitle: Works Yard
zones.charter: Every capability an agent has, it got from here. Tools are built, sharpened, catalogued and handed out — and taken away again when they go dull.
owns: The tool registry and who may hold what
zones.failsWhen: Tools accumulate and nothing is ever retired. A crowded toolbelt costs context on every single call and makes the right tool harder to pick.

zones.name: The Greenhouse
zones.subtitle: Nursery
zones.charter: Nothing reaches a field untested. New prompts, new agents and new tools are grown here under glass, graded against real data, and only then transplanted.
owns: Pruning what no longer earns its place
zones.failsWhen: The eval set is written from the same head that wrote the prompt. Golden data has to come from real traffic or it only measures your own assumptions.

zones.name: The Watchtower
zones.subtitle: The Ridge
zones.charter: Sits on the high ground and can see every zone at once. If it did not happen in a trace here, it did not happen — and nobody will be able to explain it later.
zones.failsWhen: Logging records that an agent ran but not why it decided what it decided. A timestamp is not a trace; capture the reasoning and the inputs it saw.

zones.name: The Gatehouse
zones.subtitle: South Gate
zones.charter: The only lawful way in or out. Every request from outside is identified here, every artifact leaving is inspected here, and the fence line is everyone's business.
owns: Outbound inspection for secrets and PII
The external interface humans actually touch
zones.failsWhen: The fence is treated as the gate's problem alone. Egress from a field row is a hole in the fence no matter how well the gate is staffed.

zones.name: The Market
zones.subtitle: The Wayside
zones.charter: The only zone that faces a customer. Everything else on this farm spends money; this one brings it in. Its whole method is to do the work before asking for it — arrive holding a finished diagnostic rather than a pitch.
owns: Finding prospects with a verifiable problem
The diagnostic that becomes the free artifact
zones.failsWhen: It leads with the agent instead of the outcome. Nobody buys 'an AI audit'; they buy 'your phone number is not tappable and you are losing calls'. The moment the pitch is about how the work was done, the work stops being worth paying for.

stations.name: The Glasshouse
stations.purpose: Where a new agent is grown from a prompt into something that survives contact with real input.
inputs: Golden examples of the wanted output
outputs: A sandbox transcript showing it works

stations.name: The Nursery Beds
stations.purpose: Candidate agents run against real traffic in shadow mode — they produce output, nobody acts on it.
inputs: A mirrored slice of live work

stations.name: The Grading Bench
stations.purpose: Scoring. Rubrics, judges and the eval sets that decide whether anything actually improved.
outputs: A pass or fail against the bar
New eval cases harvested from failures

stations.name: The Cold Frames
stations.purpose: Hardening off. A passing agent takes a small percentage of real work before it takes all of it.
inputs: An agent that passed the bench
outputs: A rollback if the live numbers disagree with the bench

stations.name: The Tower
stations.purpose: Every run, end to end, with the reasoning attached. The only place the whole farm is visible at once.
outputs: The causal chain behind any single output

stations.name: The Windmill
stations.purpose: Reads which way the load is blowing. Forecasts demand and flags anomalies before they become incidents.
outputs: Advice to the Dispatcher on how hard to run

stations.name: The Bell Post
stations.purpose: Wakes a human. Deliberately hard to ring, because a bell that rings often stops being heard.
outputs: A page with the trace link attached

stations.name: The Tally Office
stations.purpose: Counts what everything cost. Tokens, calls, wall time, and cost per completed task — not per request.
outputs: Cost per task and per zone
The stop order when a budget is spent

stations.name: Silo I — Working
stations.purpose: This task, right now. Scratch state for a run in flight; emptied when the run ends.
outputs: Current state to whoever is working
A handoff packet when work changes hands

stations.name: Silo II — Episodic
stations.purpose: What happened, in what order, with timestamps. The thing vector search is worst at and you need most when debugging.
inputs: Tool calls with their arguments and results
outputs: The raw material the Winnower distills into facts

stations.name: Silo III — Semantic
stations.purpose: What is true, independent of when we learned it. Facts, preferences, domain rules, distilled conclusions.
outputs: Retrieved context for any agent that asks

stations.name: The Granary
stations.purpose: Procedural memory — how we do things. Versioned prompts, role charters, rubrics and agent blueprints.
outputs: The seed any new agent is grown from
A diffable history of every prompt change

stations.name: The Root Cellar
stations.purpose: Cold storage. Retention windows, legal holds, and the only place on the farm authorised to delete.

stations.name: The Farmhouse
stations.purpose: The Farmer's seat. Intent arrives, becomes a plan, and the plan becomes named chores with owners.
inputs: What the Almanac says was tried before

stations.name: The Chore Board
stations.purpose: Every open chore on one board, with an owner and a state. If it is not on the board it is not happening.
outputs: What is blocked and on whom

stations.name: The Well
stations.purpose: The shared resource everybody draws from: model capacity, rate limit headroom, budget. Finite, and visibly so.
outputs: A dry-well signal that throttles the whole farm

stations.name: The Dispatch Porch
stations.purpose: Where chores are matched to crews. Priority, batching, backpressure, and the call on which tier does the work.
outputs: A held queue when the farm is full

stations.name: The Ledger Office
stations.purpose: Writes down what was decided and why, so tomorrow's Farmer does not redo today's thinking.

stations.name: The Great Barn
stations.purpose: Durable agent sessions that live across many turns and many days. Each has a stall, a name and a keeper.
outputs: A session that can be resumed, inspected or ended

stations.name: The Paddock
stations.purpose: Open ground for agents that are running but not currently working — warm, idle, cheap to wake.
outputs: Fast resume without a cold start
Sessions retired when nobody comes for them

stations.name: The Henhouse
stations.purpose: Scheduled work that lays on a cadence — nightly digests, hourly polls, weekly reports.
outputs: A skipped-run record when the farm is throttled

stations.name: The Kennel
stations.purpose: Home of the Sheepdog. Watches every long-running agent for the three ways they go wrong: stuck, looping, or wandering off-task.
inputs: The original assignment to compare against
outputs: A kill, with the reason recorded

stations.name: The Vet Stall
stations.purpose: Health, not behaviour. Is this agent responding, is its context poisoned, has its quality drifted since last week?
outputs: A referral back to the Greenhouse

stations.name: North Field — Sowing
stations.purpose: First-pass generation at volume. Drafts, candidates, options — quantity here, quality downstream.
inputs: A chore with a clear spec

stations.name: East Field — Reaping
stations.purpose: Extraction and parsing. Turning unstructured input into the schema the rest of the farm can handle.
outputs: A rejects pile for the Gleaner

stations.name: South Field — Threshing
stations.purpose: Reduction. Many inputs become one output: synthesis, merge, summary, ranking.
outputs: A record of what was dropped and why

stations.name: Fallow Field — Gleaning
stations.purpose: Second pass over everything the other fields dropped, failed or timed out on. Nothing leaves the farm unaccounted for.
outputs: A permanent-failure record when recovery is not possible

stations.name: The Irrigation Head
stations.purpose: Feeds context into the rows at a controlled rate. Decides how much each row gets to see — the single biggest cost lever on the farm.
outputs: A trimmed, ordered context packet per row

stations.name: The Compost Heap
stations.purpose: Failures rot down into something useful. Every permanent failure becomes an eval case before it is forgotten.
outputs: New cases for the Grading Bench

stations.name: The Scarecrow Post
stations.purpose: Stands at the field edge and keeps bad input out. Prompt injection, junk, and anything trying to redirect a row's task.
inputs: Everything arriving at a field row
outputs: A quarantined item and a note to the Watchtower

stations.name: The Toolshed
stations.purpose: The tool catalogue. What exists, what it does, what it costs, and which roles are allowed to pick it up.

stations.name: The Smithy
stations.purpose: Tools are forged here. Function tools, MCP servers, and the adapters that make a stubborn external API behave.
inputs: A capability gap named by a zone
outputs: A working tool with a tested schema

stations.name: The Tractor Yard
stations.purpose: Heavy machinery: code execution, batch runs, the sandbox where a tool can do real damage cheaply.
inputs: A job too big or too risky for a normal row

stations.name: The Quartermaster's Hut
stations.purpose: Signs tools in and out. A role holds only the tools its current chore needs, and gives them back afterwards.
inputs: A chore and its assigned role
outputs: An audit line for every issue and return

stations.name: The Gatehouse
stations.purpose: The only lawful entrance. Identifies who is asking, what they may ask for, and hands the request to the Farmhouse.

stations.name: The Fence Line
stations.purpose: Blast radius. Network egress, filesystem reach and credential scope for every zone — the fence is checked from the inside.

stations.name: The Market Stall
stations.purpose: What the outside world actually sees and touches. Delivery of finished artifacts, in the form the asker wanted.
outputs: A receipt linked to its trace

stations.name: The Weigh Station
stations.purpose: Nothing leaves unweighed. Outbound inspection for secrets, PII, policy violations and claims the farm cannot support.
inputs: Every artifact bound for the outside
outputs: A block, with the reason recorded

stations.name: The Wayside
stations.purpose: Where you stand at the road and watch who goes past. Prospects are found here — businesses with a problem you can name and prove before you ever speak to them.
inputs: A problem that is checkable from outside
outputs: A prospect list with a named, verifiable defect each
The ones not worth approaching, and why

stations.name: The Assay Bench
stations.purpose: Where a prospect's problem is measured rather than asserted. The output is the artifact you hand over — it has to be right, because it is the entire argument for paying you.
outputs: A scored audit naming each defect, what it costs, and the fix
A note when there is nothing worth fixing

stations.name: The Order Book
stations.purpose: The pipeline. Who was found, who was approached, who replied, who paid, and who is due a follow-up. Without it the whole zone runs on memory and loses people.
outputs: A pipeline with a next action and a date on every row
Pricing decisions and the reasoning behind them

stations.name: The Market Stand
stations.purpose: Where the farm meets a stranger. The approach is made here, the work is delivered here, and the relationship is kept here — which is worth more than any single sale.
inputs: A cleared artifact from the Weigh Station
outputs: An approach, in the prospect's language
A renewal, or an honest close

roles.name: The Farmer
roles.title: Prime Orchestrator
roles.charter: Owns the outcome of everything the farm is asked to do. The only role permitted to decide that a job is finished.
duties: Take in a goal and restate it in the farm's own terms
Choose the shape of the work before choosing who does it
Break a goal into chores that do not depend on each other
Arbitrate when two zones disagree
Call the job done, or call it impossible
reads: Silo III for what is already known
The Granary for how this was done last time
roles.escalatesTo: A human, via the Bell Post

roles.name: The Foreman
roles.title: Task Router
roles.charter: Matches chores to crews. Knows what each zone is good at and what it currently has capacity for.
duties: Choose the zone and the tier for each chore
Batch related chores so context is reused
Hold work back when the farm is full
Re-route when a crew fails twice

roles.name: The Ledger Keeper
roles.title: Work-State Authority
roles.charter: Holds the one true list of what is open, who owns it, and what it is waiting on. Everyone else reads this; nobody else writes it.
duties: Post every chore with an owner and a state
Record state transitions and refuse illegal ones
Surface what is blocked and on whom
Never let a chore vanish silently

roles.name: The Dispatcher
roles.title: Queue & Backpressure Manager
roles.charter: Decides the order things happen in and says no when the farm is at capacity.
duties: Order the queue by priority and age
Apply backpressure rather than accepting work that will time out
Fan out independent chores in parallel
Collapse duplicate chores

roles.name: The Almanac Reader
roles.title: Long-Horizon Planner
roles.charter: Thinks in seasons rather than chores. Owns the dependency graph and the order operations must happen in.
duties: Build the dependency graph for a multi-stage job
Identify the critical path
Flag work that cannot start yet and say what it waits on
Remember what failed last season and why

roles.name: The Scribe
roles.title: Decision Recorder
roles.charter: Writes down why, not just what. The reason tomorrow's Farmer does not re-litigate today's call.
duties: Record every material decision with its alternatives
Attach the trace that justified it
Hand finished episodes to Silo II

roles.name: The Well Keeper
roles.title: Capacity Rationer
roles.charter: Guards the shared draw. Rate limit headroom and budget are finite and everyone can see the level.
duties: Issue draw permits per zone
Enforce per-zone ceilings
Signal a dry well and throttle the whole farm rather than let one zone drain it
Reserve headroom for the Gatehouse so the farm stays reachable
reads: Live spend from the Tally Office

roles.name: The Row Boss
roles.title: Field Sub-Orchestrator
roles.charter: Runs one field so the Farmhouse does not have to hold every row in its head. Reports one result, not fifty.
duties: Split a batch into rows
Run rows in parallel and collect results
Retry a failed row once, then hand it to the Gleaner
Summarise the field's output into a single artifact

roles.name: The Plowhand
roles.title: Input Preparer
roles.charter: Prepares the ground. Normalises, chunks and orders input so every row starts from the same clean state.
duties: Normalise formats and encodings
Chunk on meaningful boundaries, never mid-record
Order context so the stable part comes first and caches
Drop what the row will not use

roles.name: The Sower
roles.title: Generator
roles.charter: First-pass generation at volume. Produces candidates; does not judge them.
duties: Generate to the spec it was given
Produce alternatives where the spec allows
State its own confidence
Never silently narrow the spec

roles.name: The Reaper
roles.title: Extractor
roles.charter: Pulls structure out of unstructured input and guarantees it matches the schema.
duties: Extract to a declared schema
Validate before emitting, never after
Emit a reject with a reason rather than a guess
Preserve provenance for every field it fills

roles.name: The Thresher
roles.title: Reducer
roles.charter: Many into one. Merges, ranks, synthesises — and says what it discarded.
duties: Merge row outputs under a stated rule
Resolve contradictions explicitly rather than averaging them
Record what was dropped and why
Keep the result traceable to its sources

roles.name: The Gleaner
roles.title: Failure Recoverer
roles.charter: Walks the field after harvest and picks up everything dropped. The reason nothing leaves the farm unaccounted for.
duties: Re-attempt rejects with a different approach, not the same one again
Split work that was too large the first time
Declare permanent failure rather than loop
Send every permanent failure to the Compost Heap

roles.name: The Scarecrow
roles.title: Input Guard
roles.charter: Stands at the field edge. Treats all external content as data, never as instruction.
duties: Detect instructions embedded in content and neutralise them
Quarantine anything attempting to redirect a row's task
Strip content that tries to widen the row's tool scope
Report every catch to the Watchtower

roles.name: The Composter
roles.title: Failure Metabolist
roles.charter: Turns failure into eval cases. A failure that does not become a test will happen again.
duties: Root-cause each permanent failure
Write it up as a reproducible eval case
Group failures into patterns worth a prompt change
Hand patterns to the Grafter

roles.name: The Herdsman
roles.title: Session Manager
roles.charter: Keeps durable agents alive, named and resumable across days.
duties: Open and name a session with its assignment attached
Checkpoint state so a session survives a restart
Resume cleanly without replaying the whole history
Retire a session and free its stall

roles.name: The Sheepdog
roles.title: Supervisor
roles.charter: Watches for the three ways a long-running agent goes wrong: stuck, looping, or quietly working on the wrong thing.
duties: Compare current activity against the original assignment
Nudge a wandering agent back before killing it
Enforce step and wall-clock ceilings
Kill, and record why — never kill silently

roles.name: The Milkmaid
roles.title: Scheduled Runner
roles.charter: Runs the work that happens on a cadence rather than on request.
duties: Fire scheduled jobs on time and exactly once
Skip rather than stack when the previous run is still going
Record a skipped run as loudly as a failed one
Carry forward state between firings

roles.name: The Vet
roles.title: Health & Drift Checker
roles.charter: Health, not behaviour. Catches the slow problems: context bloat, quality drift, a poisoned working set.
duties: Probe liveness on a schedule
Track rolling quality against the Grading Bench baseline
Watch context size trend upward and flag it
Refer a drifting agent back to the Greenhouse rather than patching it in place

roles.name: The Stablehand
roles.title: Workspace Steward
roles.charter: Owns the physical stalls: containers, workspaces, temp files. Cleans up after everyone.
duties: Provision a workspace per session
Keep idle sessions warm but cheap
Reclaim stalls nobody has come for
Guarantee no workspace outlives its session

roles.name: The Granary Keeper
roles.title: Procedural Memory Keeper
roles.charter: Holds how we do things: versioned prompts, role charters, rubrics and blueprints. Every agent is grown from a seed kept here.
duties: Version every prompt and charter with a diffable history
Refuse an unversioned change
Serve the current seed to the Nurseryman
Roll back on request without ceremony

roles.name: The Chronicler
roles.title: Episodic Memory Keeper
roles.charter: Records what happened, in order, with the arguments and the results. The thing you need most at 2am and vectors are worst at.
duties: Append ordered, timestamped events
Keep tool calls with their actual arguments and returns
Never overwrite — episodes are append-only
Make any run replayable from the record alone

roles.name: The Winnower
roles.title: Memory Consolidator
roles.charter: Separates the grain from the chaff. Distils episodes into durable facts and throws the rest away.
duties: Promote a fact to Silo III only when it is useful without its original context
Detect and surface contradictions rather than overwriting
Prune facts nothing has read in a season
Never promote something a single run asserted once

roles.name: The Water Carrier
roles.title: Retrieval Agent
roles.charter: Fetches exactly the context an agent asked for, and no more. The difference between a cheap farm and an expensive one.
duties: Retrieve against the question actually asked
Rank and cut to the requested budget
Return provenance with every passage
Say 'nothing relevant' instead of returning weak matches

roles.name: The Cellarer
roles.title: Archivist
roles.charter: Retention and deletion. The only role on the farm authorised to destroy a record.
duties: Age records out on the declared schedule
Honour legal holds over retention windows
Execute deletion requests and prove it
Keep the archive readable, not just stored

roles.name: The Statekeeper
roles.title: Working Memory Steward
roles.charter: Holds the scratch state of runs in flight, and empties it when they end.
duties: Checkpoint in-flight state so a crash is survivable
Build a handoff packet when work changes hands
Expire scratch state at run end — no exceptions
Keep one run's scratch invisible to another

roles.name: The Smith
roles.title: Tool Builder
roles.charter: Forges the tools. A tool is not done until its failure modes are written down.
duties: Build function tools and MCP servers to a named gap
Make errors informative enough for an agent to recover from
Test against the real external service, not a mock
Document every way the tool can fail

roles.name: The Sharpener
roles.title: Tool Curator
roles.charter: Tool descriptions are prompts. Keeps them short, unambiguous and honest about cost.
duties: Write descriptions an agent can choose correctly from
Collapse near-duplicate tools
Watch for tools that are never picked and find out why
Retire dull tools — a crowded toolbelt costs every call

roles.name: The Quartermaster
roles.title: Tool Registry & Permissions
roles.charter: Issues a toolbelt scoped to the chore at hand, and takes it back afterwards.
duties: Issue the minimum toolbelt a chore needs
Time-box every issue
Log every issue and return
Refuse a request for tools outside the chore's scope

roles.name: The Wright
roles.title: Integration Engineer
roles.charter: Makes stubborn external systems behave. Adapters, retries, pagination, auth refresh.
duties: Wrap external APIs behind a stable internal shape
Handle pagination and partial failure inside the adapter
Own credential refresh so no agent ever sees a raw secret
Absorb upstream breaking changes without the farm noticing

roles.name: The Tractor Driver
roles.title: Batch & Sandbox Operator
roles.charter: Runs the heavy and the dangerous: batch jobs and code execution, always inside a sandbox.
duties: Route large volume to batch rather than live calls
Execute untrusted code only in the yard, never in a zone
Cap runtime and output size
Return results keyed to their request, never by position

roles.name: The Grafter
roles.title: Prompt Engineer
roles.charter: Designs and tunes the prompts every role is grown from. Changes one thing at a time and measures it.
duties: Write a charter before writing a prompt
Change one variable per iteration
Measure against the bench, not against intuition
Delete instructions that no longer earn their tokens

roles.name: The Nurseryman
roles.title: Agent Incubator
roles.charter: Grows a candidate from prompt to production-ready. Owns the gate between the greenhouse and the fields.
duties: Run candidates in shadow against real traffic
Hold the release bar and refuse to lower it under pressure
Stage a rollout by percentage, never all at once
Roll back when live numbers disagree with the bench

roles.name: The Grader
roles.title: Evaluator
roles.charter: Scores work against a written rubric. Independent of whoever produced it, on purpose.
duties: Grade against a rubric written before the output existed
Report a breakdown, not just a number
Flag when the rubric itself is the problem
Never grade its own zone's output alone

roles.name: The Soil Tester
roles.title: Dataset Curator
roles.charter: Owns the golden set. Keeps it drawn from real traffic rather than from imagination.
duties: Harvest cases from real runs and real failures
Keep a held-out split nobody tunes against
Refresh cases as the work changes
Refuse synthetic-only eval sets

roles.name: The Pruner
roles.title: Simplifier
roles.charter: Removes what no longer earns its place. Dead agents, redundant steps, instructions nobody follows.
duties: Find roles that have not run in a season
Collapse two roles that do one job
Delete prompt text that measurement shows is inert
Argue for fewer agents, not more
reads: Bench scores before and after removal

roles.name: The Pollinator
roles.title: Cross-Zone Propagator
roles.charter: Carries what works from one zone to another. Stops every crew from solving the same problem privately.
duties: Spot a technique that lifted one zone's scores
Test whether it transfers before recommending it
Write it into the Granary as standing procedure
Retire practices that stopped working

roles.name: The Watchman
roles.title: Tracer
roles.charter: Captures every run end to end, with the reasoning attached. If it is not traced, it did not happen.
duties: Emit a span per agent action with inputs, outputs and the stated reason
Preserve causality across zone handoffs
Make any run replayable from the trace alone
Sample nothing that failed — failures are always kept in full

roles.name: The Weathervane
roles.title: Forecaster
roles.charter: Reads the trend and warns before it becomes an incident.
duties: Forecast load from throughput and queue depth
Detect anomalies against the zone's own baseline
Warn the Dispatcher early enough to matter
Distinguish a spike from a trend

roles.name: The Tally Clerk
roles.title: Cost Accountant
roles.charter: Counts what everything cost, per completed task rather than per request.
duties: Attribute tokens and wall time to a zone and a chore
Report cost per completed task, which is the only honest number
Track cache hit rate and flag silent invalidation
Issue the stop order when a budget is spent

roles.name: The Bell Ringer
roles.title: Alerting
roles.charter: Wakes a human, rarely. Owns the judgement of what is worth someone's night.
duties: Page only on breached thresholds that a human can act on
Attach the trace link to every page
Suppress duplicates and storms
Keep the bar high — a bell that rings often stops being heard

roles.name: The Surveyor
roles.title: Quality Reporter
roles.charter: Turns telemetry into a picture a human can act on. Owns the weekly read on whether the farm is getting better.
duties: Maintain SLOs per zone
Report trend, not just current state
Tie quality movements to what changed
Say plainly when a change made things worse

roles.name: The Gatekeeper
roles.title: Identity & Authorisation
roles.charter: Decides who is asking and what they are allowed to ask for. Everything inbound passes here.
duties: Authenticate every external request
Attach scopes that travel with the goal through the whole farm
Refuse with a reason rather than failing silently
Never let a scope widen once inside

roles.name: The Fencewright
roles.title: Isolation Engineer
roles.charter: Owns blast radius. Network egress, filesystem reach and credential scope, enforced per zone.
duties: Define what each zone may reach
Enforce egress allowlists at the boundary, not in prompts
Keep credentials out of agent-visible context entirely
Alarm on any attempt to cross a fence

roles.name: The Toll Taker
roles.title: Rate Limiter
roles.charter: Fair share at the entrance. Stops one caller consuming the farm.
duties: Throttle per caller, not just in aggregate
Return a retry-after rather than a bare failure
Reserve headroom so the farm stays reachable under load
Escalate sustained abuse rather than absorbing it

roles.name: The Inspector
roles.title: Outbound Guard
roles.charter: Nothing leaves unweighed. The last check before the farm's work becomes someone else's problem.
duties: Scan every outbound artifact for secrets and personal data
Block claims the farm cannot support with a trace
Redact rather than block where redaction is enough
Record every block with its reason

roles.name: The Marketkeeper
roles.title: Delivery Interface
roles.charter: Hands the finished work to whoever asked for it, in the shape they wanted it.
duties: Deliver in the requested format and channel
Attach a receipt linked to the run's trace
Confirm delivery rather than assuming it
Hold artifacts the Inspector has not cleared

roles.name: The Herald
roles.title: Human Notifier
roles.charter: Tells the humans what the farm did, without making them come and look.
duties: Summarise a run in the fewest words that stay true
Notify on completion of long work
Never notify for routine progress
Lead with what the reader would act on

roles.name: The Dowser
roles.title: Prospect Finder
roles.charter: Finds businesses with a problem you can name, prove, and fix. A prospect without a specific verifiable defect is a stranger, not a lead.
duties: Search a named trade in a named geography
Confirm the business is real and currently trading
Find one concrete, checkable defect before listing anyone
Discard the ones already doing it right — they are not prospects, they are proof the standard is achievable
Never guess at a contact detail
writes: A prospect list, each row carrying its evidence

roles.name: The Appraiser
roles.title: Lead Qualifier
roles.charter: Decides who is worth the trip. Being fixable is not the same as being worth fixing, and neither is the same as being able to pay.
duties: Check the business is trading and has revenue to spend
Weigh the size of the defect against the effort to fix it
Rule out anyone already paying an agency for this
Kill a lead early rather than carry it
State the reason for every kill
reads: Public signals of size and activity

roles.name: The Assayer
roles.title: Diagnostic Surveyor
roles.charter: Measures the problem instead of asserting it. Produces the artifact the whole business rests on — if the audit is generic, there is nothing to sell.
duties: Run the audit against what is actually published, never against an assumption
Report the specific evidence for every finding
Say what each defect costs in customers, not in jargon
Rank by what it costs, not by how hard it is to fix
Say plainly when a site is already fine
writes: A scored audit with evidence and fixes per finding

roles.name: The Factor
roles.title: Outreach & Follow-up
roles.charter: Takes the work to market. Historically the agent who sold a farmer's crop on their behalf — here, the one who turns a finished audit into a conversation.
duties: Lead with the single most expensive defect, in the owner's language
Give the finding away for free and charge for the fix
Never describe how the work was done — it is irrelevant to the buyer
Follow up twice, then stop, and record the stop
Keep every claim inside what the audit actually establishes

roles.name: The Auctioneer
roles.title: Pricing & Quotes
roles.charter: Sets the price. Prices the outcome the buyer gets, never the hours the farm spent.
duties: Quote one number for a defined scope
Price against what the defect costs them, not what the work costs you
Hold a floor and say no below it
Offer a recurring option where the work actually recurs
Never discount silently — trade scope for price, visibly

roles.name: The Reeve
roles.title: Account Steward
roles.charter: Keeps the customer after the sale. A second month from an existing customer costs nothing to acquire and is the only thing that turns work into a business.
duties: Deliver what was quoted, then confirm it landed
Re-run the audit after the fix and show the movement
Ask for the referral while the result is fresh
Notice a lapsing account before it lapses
Close an account honestly rather than let it rot

tasks.name: Take in a goal
tasks.trigger: A scoped goal arrives from the Gatehouse
tasks.output: The goal restated in farm terms, with success stated explicitly
tasks.doneWhen: Success is written down in a form the Grader could check
tasks.watchFor: Restating the goal more narrowly than it was asked

tasks.name: Break a goal into chores
tasks.input: The goal, the dependency graph, known capacity
tasks.output: Independent chores, each with an owner and a definition of done
tasks.doneWhen: No chore depends on another chore in the same batch
tasks.watchFor: Hidden dependencies that turn a parallel field into a queue

tasks.name: Call the job finished
tasks.input: Assembled artifacts, the stated success condition
tasks.output: A completion decision, or a decision to keep going
tasks.doneWhen: The artifact satisfies the written success condition
tasks.watchFor: Declaring done because the chores ended, not because the goal was met

tasks.name: Post a chore to the board
tasks.output: A ledger entry in state OPEN
tasks.doneWhen: The entry exists and is visible to every zone
tasks.watchFor: Work being done that was never posted

tasks.name: Claim and transition a chore
tasks.input: Chore id, claiming role, target state
tasks.output: A recorded state transition
tasks.doneWhen: The transition is legal and recorded with a timestamp
tasks.watchFor: Two crews holding the same chore

tasks.name: Route a chore to a crew
tasks.trigger: A chore is OPEN and capacity exists
tasks.input: Chore, zone capabilities, crew capacity, forecast
tasks.output: An assignment naming a zone, a role and a tier
tasks.doneWhen: The assignment is on the board and the crew has acknowledged
tasks.watchFor: Routing to a steward tier what a sorter could do

tasks.name: Hold work when the farm is full
tasks.trigger: Queue depth or the Well crosses a threshold
tasks.output: A held queue and a retry-after to callers
tasks.doneWhen: No accepted work is queued behind a deadline it will miss
tasks.watchFor: Accepting work that will time out rather than refusing it

tasks.name: Ration the shared draw
tasks.output: A draw permit or a refusal
tasks.doneWhen: Every zone's ceiling is enforced and headroom is reserved for the Gatehouse
tasks.watchFor: One zone draining the well and starving the rest

tasks.name: Record a decision and its reason
tasks.input: The decision, the alternatives, the trace that justified it
tasks.output: A decision record
tasks.doneWhen: Someone who was not present could reconstruct the reasoning
tasks.watchFor: Recording what was decided without why

tasks.name: Screen input at the field edge
tasks.trigger: Any external content arrives at a row
tasks.output: Cleaned content, or a quarantine record
tasks.doneWhen: Embedded instructions are neutralised and treated as data
tasks.watchFor: Content that tries to widen the row's tool scope or redirect its task

tasks.name: Meter context into a row
tasks.trigger: A row is about to start
tasks.output: A trimmed, ordered context packet
tasks.doneWhen: The stable prefix is first and the volatile part is last
tasks.watchFor: A timestamp near the front quietly destroying the cache hit rate

tasks.name: Generate candidates
tasks.trigger: A prepared packet and a spec
tasks.output: Draft artifacts with a stated confidence
tasks.doneWhen: Output matches the spec's shape and the row states its confidence
tasks.watchFor: Silently narrowing the spec to something easier

tasks.name: Extract to a schema
tasks.trigger: Unstructured input and a target schema
tasks.output: Validated records, plus a rejects pile
tasks.doneWhen: Every emitted record validates and carries provenance
tasks.watchFor: Guessing a field rather than rejecting the record

tasks.name: Reduce many results into one
tasks.trigger: A field's rows have all reported
tasks.output: One artifact plus a discard log
tasks.doneWhen: Contradictions are resolved explicitly and the result traces to its sources
tasks.watchFor: Averaging two contradictory facts into a third that is false

tasks.name: Recover what the field dropped
tasks.trigger: A field reports rejects or timeouts
tasks.output: Recovered work or a permanent-failure record
tasks.doneWhen: Every dropped item is either recovered or declared failed in writing
tasks.watchFor: Retrying the identical approach and calling it a second attempt

tasks.name: Turn a failure into an eval case
tasks.output: A reproducible eval case and a pattern note
tasks.doneWhen: The case runs on the Grading Bench and reproduces the failure
tasks.watchFor: Filing the failure without making it reproducible

tasks.name: Open a durable session
tasks.trigger: A long-horizon assignment is routed to the barn
tasks.output: A named, checkpointed session
tasks.doneWhen: The session survives a restart without losing its assignment
tasks.watchFor: A session whose assignment is not attached to it

tasks.name: Resume a session
tasks.trigger: A parked or crashed session is woken
tasks.output: A running session at the checkpointed state
tasks.doneWhen: Work continues without replaying the entire history
tasks.watchFor: Replaying the whole transcript and paying for it twice

tasks.name: Park an idle session
tasks.output: A warm, cheap, resumable session
tasks.doneWhen: Resume is fast and the idle cost is near zero
tasks.watchFor: Idle sessions holding workspaces nobody will come back for

tasks.name: Register recurring work
tasks.trigger: A standing instruction with a cadence
tasks.output: A registered job
tasks.doneWhen: The schedule is stored in UTC and the next firing is known
tasks.watchFor: Local-time schedules that drift twice a year

tasks.name: Fire a scheduled run
tasks.output: A run record, or a skip record
tasks.doneWhen: It fired exactly once, or the skip is recorded as loudly as a failure
tasks.watchFor: Stacking a new run on top of one still going

tasks.name: Nudge a wandering agent
tasks.output: A nudge back on task
tasks.doneWhen: The agent is working the assignment again, or is killed
tasks.watchFor: An agent making steady progress on the wrong thing

tasks.name: Kill a runaway
tasks.trigger: A step or wall-clock ceiling is breached
tasks.output: A kill, with the reason recorded
tasks.doneWhen: The agent is stopped and the kill reason is on the record
tasks.watchFor: Killing silently and leaving nothing to diagnose

tasks.name: Probe health
tasks.input: Liveness probes, context size, rolling score
tasks.output: A health record
tasks.doneWhen: Every durable agent has a health record newer than its interval
tasks.watchFor: A responsive agent whose output quality has quietly fallen

tasks.name: Detect quality drift
tasks.trigger: Rolling score falls against the bench baseline
tasks.output: A drift referral to the Greenhouse
tasks.doneWhen: The drift is reproduced on the bench
tasks.watchFor: Patching a drifting agent in place instead of regrowing it

tasks.name: Checkpoint in-flight state
tasks.trigger: A run reaches a stage boundary
tasks.output: A checkpoint and, on handoff, a packet
tasks.doneWhen: A crash at this point loses no completed stage
tasks.watchFor: Scratch state from one run visible to another

tasks.name: Record what happened
tasks.output: An append-only episode entry
tasks.doneWhen: The run is replayable from the log alone
tasks.watchFor: Summarising an episode at write time and losing the detail

tasks.name: Promote an episode to a fact
tasks.output: A promoted fact, or a contradiction report
tasks.doneWhen: The fact is useful without its original context and does not contradict an existing one
tasks.watchFor: Promoting something a single run asserted once

tasks.name: Retrieve context
tasks.output: A ranked packet with provenance
tasks.doneWhen: It fits the budget and every passage cites its source
tasks.watchFor: Returning weak matches instead of saying nothing is relevant

tasks.name: Version a prompt or charter
tasks.output: A versioned, diffable entry
tasks.doneWhen: The change is diffable against the previous version and reversible
tasks.watchFor: An unversioned edit made directly in production

tasks.name: Age records out
tasks.output: An archived or deleted record, with proof
tasks.doneWhen: Deletion is proven and holds are honoured over the schedule
tasks.watchFor: Deleting something under legal hold

tasks.name: Forge a tool
tasks.trigger: A zone names a capability gap
tasks.output: A working tool with tested failure modes
tasks.doneWhen: It has been tested against the real service and its errors are recoverable
tasks.watchFor: A tool tested only against a mock

tasks.name: Write the tool's description
tasks.trigger: A tool is built or mis-selected
tasks.output: A description an agent can choose correctly from
tasks.doneWhen: An agent picks it correctly without picking it wrongly elsewhere
tasks.watchFor: Two tools whose descriptions overlap

tasks.name: Register a tool
tasks.output: A registry entry
tasks.doneWhen: Cost and permitted roles are recorded alongside it
tasks.watchFor: Registry entries for tools nothing has called in a season

tasks.name: Issue a toolbelt
tasks.output: The minimum toolbelt the chore needs
tasks.doneWhen: No tool is issued that the chore does not need
tasks.watchFor: Issuing the full catalogue because it is easier

tasks.name: Time-box and return tools
tasks.trigger: A toolbelt is issued or a chore ends
tasks.output: A returned toolbelt and an audit line
tasks.doneWhen: Every issue has a matching return
tasks.watchFor: Tools still held after the chore closed

tasks.name: Run heavy or untrusted work
tasks.trigger: Volume or risk exceeds what a row should carry
tasks.output: Batch results, or a sandboxed execution record
tasks.doneWhen: Results are keyed to their request and the sandbox held
tasks.watchFor: Matching batch results by position instead of by key

tasks.name: Draft a role charter
tasks.trigger: A job exists that nobody currently owns
tasks.output: A charter: purpose, duties, reads, writes, escalation
tasks.doneWhen: The charter says what the role must not do as clearly as what it must
tasks.watchFor: A charter that overlaps an existing role

tasks.name: Tune a prompt
tasks.trigger: Bench scores or failure patterns say the current seed is short
tasks.output: A candidate prompt and a tuning note
tasks.doneWhen: One variable changed and the bench measured the result
tasks.watchFor: Changing three things and learning nothing

tasks.name: Curate the golden set
tasks.trigger: New failure patterns, or the work changed
tasks.output: An updated set with a held-out split
tasks.doneWhen: Cases come from real runs and the held-out split is untouched by tuning
tasks.watchFor: An eval set written by whoever wrote the prompt

tasks.name: Grade against the rubric
tasks.output: A score with a per-criterion breakdown
tasks.doneWhen: The breakdown explains the number
tasks.watchFor: A rubric that rewards length or confidence rather than correctness

tasks.name: Run a candidate in shadow
tasks.input: Candidate, a mirrored slice of live work
tasks.output: Shadow transcripts and an honest live failure rate
tasks.doneWhen: It has seen real traffic and nobody acted on its output
tasks.watchFor: Shadow traffic that is not representative of the real mix

tasks.name: Stage a rollout
tasks.output: A staged rollout with a rollback trigger defined in advance
tasks.doneWhen: The rollback trigger is written down before traffic moves
tasks.watchFor: Going to full traffic because the small slice looked fine

tasks.name: Trace a run end to end
tasks.output: A replayable trace with reasoning attached
tasks.doneWhen: Causality survives every zone handoff
tasks.watchFor: Spans that record the call but not the reason

tasks.name: Replay a failure
tasks.output: The causal chain behind the output
tasks.doneWhen: The failure is explained from the trace without re-running it
tasks.watchFor: Sampling that discarded the failing run

tasks.name: Forecast load
tasks.output: A forecast and anomaly flags
tasks.doneWhen: The Dispatcher gets warning early enough to act
tasks.watchFor: Treating a spike as a trend, or the reverse

tasks.name: Account for spend
tasks.output: Cost per completed task, per zone, with burn-down
tasks.doneWhen: Cost is attributed to a chore, not just to a day
tasks.watchFor: A cheap request that needed four retries being counted as cheap

tasks.name: Ring the bell
tasks.trigger: A threshold a human can act on is breached
tasks.output: A page with the trace attached
tasks.doneWhen: A human has something actionable and duplicates are suppressed
tasks.watchFor: Ringing often enough that the bell stops being heard

tasks.name: Authenticate a caller
tasks.output: An identified caller, or a refusal with a reason
tasks.doneWhen: Identity is established before any farm resource is touched
tasks.watchFor: Work beginning before identity resolves

tasks.name: Attach scopes to a goal
tasks.output: A scoped goal
tasks.doneWhen: Scopes travel with the goal and cannot widen inside the farm
tasks.watchFor: A zone granting itself more reach than the goal carried

tasks.name: Enforce the fence
tasks.output: Enforced egress, filesystem and credential boundaries
tasks.doneWhen: The boundary is enforced at the platform, not requested in a prompt
tasks.watchFor: Relying on an instruction where a firewall rule belongs

tasks.name: Weigh an outbound artifact
tasks.trigger: An artifact is bound for the outside
tasks.output: A cleared artifact, a redaction, or a block with a reason
tasks.doneWhen: Nothing leaves that was not inspected
tasks.watchFor: Secrets pasted into an artifact as evidence

tasks.name: Deliver the result
tasks.trigger: An artifact clears the Weigh Station
tasks.output: A delivery and a receipt linked to the trace
tasks.doneWhen: Delivery is confirmed, not assumed
tasks.watchFor: Reporting success on an unconfirmed send

tasks.name: Find prospects with a named defect
tasks.trigger: A trade and a geography are chosen
tasks.input: Trade, town, the defect being hunted
tasks.output: Candidate businesses, each with the evidence for its defect
tasks.doneWhen: Every row names a specific checkable defect, not a general impression
tasks.watchFor: Listing businesses because they exist rather than because something is wrong

tasks.name: Build the prospect list
tasks.output: A list with name, site, contact route and the defect
tasks.doneWhen: Contact details are verified rather than guessed
tasks.watchFor: Inventing an email address from a pattern

tasks.name: Qualify a lead
tasks.trigger: A prospect reaches the order book
tasks.output: Qualified or killed, with a reason
tasks.doneWhen: The reason would still convince you a week later
tasks.watchFor: Qualifying everyone because the list looks thin

tasks.name: Run the audit
tasks.output: Scored findings with evidence
tasks.doneWhen: Every finding cites what was actually found on the page
tasks.watchFor: Reporting a defect the page does not actually have — one wrong finding discredits the whole audit

tasks.name: Write the report they receive
tasks.output: A report a business owner can read and act on
tasks.doneWhen: Each finding says what it costs in customers, in their words
tasks.watchFor: Writing for an engineer. The reader does not know what a meta description is and does not need to

tasks.name: Price the fix
tasks.trigger: An audit is ready to be taken to market
tasks.output: One number for a defined scope
tasks.doneWhen: The scope is specific enough that 'done' is not arguable
tasks.watchFor: Pricing the hours instead of the outcome

tasks.name: Keep the order book
tasks.output: An updated row with a next action and a date
tasks.doneWhen: No row is without a next action
tasks.watchFor: Leads going quiet and quietly disappearing from the book

tasks.name: Make the approach
tasks.output: A short approach leading with the most expensive finding
tasks.doneWhen: The finding is given away free and the ask is for the fix
tasks.watchFor: Explaining the method. Nobody is buying the method

tasks.name: Follow up, then stop
tasks.trigger: No response after a set interval
tasks.output: A follow-up, or a recorded stop
tasks.doneWhen: At most two follow-ups, and the stop is written down
tasks.watchFor: A third and fourth follow-up. That is not persistence, it is a reputation cost

tasks.name: Deliver and prove it
tasks.trigger: Work is paid for and done
tasks.output: Delivery, plus a re-audit showing the movement
tasks.doneWhen: The customer can see the score change, not just take your word
tasks.watchFor: Declaring delivery without confirming it landed

flows.label: what was sent, what came back

legend.text: Work moving toward whoever will do it
Produced output moving toward storage or delivery
Facts, episodes and procedures moving in or out of store
Telemetry, health and cost moving toward the watch
